items.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016
items.q: you could wind up on a gig and all of a sudden in walks Ernie Watts

ctx.x: So you are predominantly a bassist and a singer, and you also are a songwriter. I’ve seen you playing guitar on the internet. All those things together, if you look at your week, a typical week now or 20 years ago, what was a typical week like for you?

Well a typical week, it all depends on what years we’re talking about. When I first got to L.A. in the late 70s, actually most of my career I’ve spent probably the most time playing the bass and singing. That’s what I got hired for and that’s what I kind of built my reputation on. But all along the way I’ve also played guitar and I play piano a little bit, enough to accompany myself. I would never book myself as a guitarist per se, but I kind of played James Taylor style, that kind of thing. But a typical week…

We might as well — we can go there now. Because right on my page here I have “record labels.” And I wanted to ask what that was like because in the 80s I was in a band that was trying for that. There’s this term that we I think probably you’ve used too in the back of your mind like, “I want to make it big.” “I want to make it in the music business.” And it used to be all right, you have to hook up with a record label.
